A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and complete 44-page documents, including appendix Sections 7–13. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of equations, proofs, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian-approximation simulations, sensitivity analyses, and attack-detection experiments, including MNIST results in Section 13.2.1.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Sections 4, 12, and 13, including the attack-detection outcomes in Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the Aggr-GA and Client-GA constructions, and Algorithm 2's Gaussian-bootstrap attack-detection procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same federated random-effects simulations and MNIST label-flipping experiment, with unchanged tasks, data coverage, and attack scenarios.

E2.justification: Figure 3 and Section 12.7 retain the same comparisons among Aggr-GA, Client-GA, and the Brownian-motion approximation based on functional CLT.

E3.justification: Simulation settings and evaluation metrics are identical. The MNIST protocol also retains five clients, PCA to three components, 200 iterations, and an attack at iteration 50.

E4.justification: The analyses of client count, iteration count, heterogeneity, synchronization, network connectivity, and attack severity remain unchanged, including both ablation tables in Section 12.7.

E5.justification: Repeated-run disclosures, including 1,000 Monte Carlo repetitions in Section 12.1.2, are unchanged. Tables 4–5 retain the same mean and 95% confidence-interval reporting.

E6.justification: All experimental plots and numerical tables are unchanged. For example, Table 5 reports the same MNIST detection probability of 0.90 and no-attack false-positive rate of 0.06.

T1.justification: Proposition 2 now explicitly repeats the definition B_{s,t} = sum_{j=s}^t A_s^j already present in Equation (10.21) in v2. Section 8.1.1 replaces R_t with the existing iterate matrix Θ_t. These are notation clarifications; the linearization, assumptions, mathematical bounds, and proof arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about Berry-Esseen bounds, time-uniform Gaussian approximations, computation-communication trade-offs, and bootstrap-based inference.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the empirical trends and the approximation methods' privacy, computation, and synchronization trade-offs are unchanged, as are applicability qualifications and future-work statements.

D1.justification: The data-generation details, step sizes, preprocessing, bootstrap settings, and warm-start description are unchanged. Section 4 also retains the same code-repository link.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, bibliography, and positioning relative to prior Gaussian-approximation and federated-learning research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes local appendix notation and punctuation edits, including the Θ_t correction, the repeated B_{s,t} definition in Proposition 2, and a missing closing parenthesis. Date and version text are updated; the narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Appendix matrix typography and equation spacing change, and existing proof material reflows across pages 34–37. Figures 1–4 and all tables retain their appearance and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves appendix readability through consistent iterate-matrix notation and an explicit definition within Proposition 2. These local clarifications make the exposition easier to follow, while the substantive theory, empirical support, and conclusions remain unchanged.
